instructions: Put 1/3 cup of the dried wood ear mushrooms in a bowl and cover them with hot water. Leave them to soak for 15 to 20 minutes, until they're soft.

Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you serve.
Meanwhile, slice the chicken thinly across the grain, about 1/4 inch thick. Toss it with 1 tbsp of the fish sauce and the 1/4 tsp white pepper.
Peel the ginger and cut it into thin matchsticks. That should be about 3/4 cup.
Cut the onion into thick wedges and chop the garlic. Cut 4 of the green onions into 1 1/2 inch lengths. Slice the Thai chilies into a small bowl for the table.
In a small bowl, stir together 3 tbsp oyster sauce, the remaining 1 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tsp dark soy sauce, 2 tsp sugar and 2 tbsp of water.
Drain the mushrooms and squeeze out the water. Cut off any hard knobs and slice them into strips.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Add half the chicken, spread it out and leave it alone for 1 minute, until it's browned underneath.
Stir fry for 1 to 2 minutes, until there's no pink left when you cut the thickest piece. Transfer it to a plate.
Add 1 tbsp of the oil and cook the rest of the chicken the same way.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil and the onion. Stir fry for 2 minutes, until the edges start to brown.
Add the ginger and mushrooms and stir fry for 1 minute. Add the garlic and stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Return the chicken and its juices to the pan and pour in the sauce. Toss for about 1 minute, until it bubbles and turns glossy.
Take the pan off the heat. Add the green onions and toss until they just wilt.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt.
Serve over the rice with the sliced chilies on the side.
method_notes: All the versions stir fry thinly sliced chicken with a lot of fresh ginger, onion and garlic in a sauce of oyster sauce, fish sauce, soy and a little sugar, and finish with green onions. The Wanderlust Kitchen (the lead) uses chicken breast and no mushrooms; Marion's Kitchen uses thighs, white pepper and wood ear mushrooms, and ImportFood uses soaked dried shiitake and a splash of stock. This one follows the lead's sauce, uses thighs and wood ear mushrooms like Marion's Kitchen, and keeps the chilies at the table. Marion's Kitchen shows 4.8 stars from 12 reviews, which is a review count, not a rating count, so it is listed without one.
